claims.explanation: K-strophanthidin is a cardiac glycoside that inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase (ATP1A1), and its selectivity across cancer cell lines is likely driven by the dependence of certain tumor cells on the Na+/K+-ATPase and associated signaling pathways. The drug's anticancer activity has been linked to DNA damage response (DDR) and KRAS-mutant lung cancer, suggesting that cells with defects in DDR or activated RAS/MAPK signaling may be more sensitive. Additionally, high expression of ATP1A1 or its interaction partners could predict sensitivity, while protective features may include expression of drug efflux pumps or alternative ion transporters.

features.basis: Target of K-strophanthidin; higher expression may increase drug binding and inhibition
KRAS-mutant lung cancers sensitive to cardiac glycosides via DDR pathway
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in selectively killed lines, suggesting defective DDR enhances sensitivity
ATM mutations observed in sensitive lines; DDR defects may potentiate cardiac glycoside-induced DNA damage
PIK3CA mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines, possibly linking PI3K/AKT signaling to Na+/K+-ATPase dependence
BRAF mutations in sensitive melanoma and colorectal lines, suggesting MAPK pathway activation may increase sensitivity
NF1 mutations in sensitive lines; NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, potentially mimicking KRAS-mutant sensitivity
SMARCA4 mutations in sensitive lines; chromatin remodeling defects may alter DDR and drug response
ARID1A mutations in sensitive lines; SWI/SNF complex mutations may impair DNA repair
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are among least affected, suggesting EGFR activation may confer resistance
PTEN mutations appear in several least affected lines (ZR751, UACC62, KALS1, FTC133), possibly indicating PI3K/AKT-driven resistance
CTNNB1 mutations in least affected lines (HEC265, KE39), suggesting Wnt/β-catenin signaling may protect against cardiac glycoside toxicity
